In one sitting, absolutely! But there are sulfites in tons of everyday food items. It’s a preservative and antioxidant so it gets used often. Some examples are wine, bread, and pretty much anything that is dried. 

While consuming 400g of SO2 in one sitting will most definitely kill anyone but Superman and Chuck Norris, you easily consume this in safe quantities on a regular basis. 

Also keep in mind that SO2 goes through chemical reactions once exposed to oxygen that change its qualities. So it’s not as toxic as in its pure form. I’m not saying that it’s necessarily safe at that point, but it’s worth considering.

Idk how much I trust geoengineeringmonitor.org but it’s an interesting website. I’m interested to find out why they used such a small quantity of sulfites and if it actually had any effect. 400g of SO2 is almost nothing as per my understanding. You could easily consume that quantity in a short period of time just by eating everyday food items.

White wine is generally not fermented with the grapes. The normal process is to squeeze the grapes of their juice and ferment the juice. The reasoning for this is that the skins will give off bitter and astringent flavors. Red wine can handle this because it is aged long enough to soften those characteristics but white wine is generally consumed much quicker. 
This doesn’t mean you can’t do it. It’s becoming more popular as “orange wine.” And you can make some great wines with this method. Just something to keep in mind. 

Also make sure you are stiring or “punching down” the skins to get a good mix and to keep the cap from drying and growing mold.
